chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot the Dhuhr prayer until the time for Asr prayer entered. He said: 'He should begin with Dhuhr, and likewise the prayers begin with the one he forgot, unless he fears that the time for that prayer will expire, in which case he begins with the one whose time is current, then he makes up the one he forgot.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct order for making up a missed Dhuhr prayer if one realizes it during the time of Asr?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural priority in *Qada* (making up missed prayers), establishing that the missed Dhuhr must be performed before Asr to maintain the chronological order of obligations. However, it introduces a pragmatic exception: if there is a genuine fear that the time for Dhuhr will expire before the worshipper can complete it, one should prioritize the current Asr prayer to ensure it is not missed entirely. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing the strict preservation of prayer times with the practical realities of human forgetfulness.
